title: The aggregation pipeline
idea: An aggregation pipeline is an ordered list of stages. Each stage takes the documents from the one before, changes them, and passes the result on.
points: `Book.aggregate(stages)` takes an array; each element is one stage.
`$match` keeps the documents that fit a condition, as `find` does.
`$group` builds one output document per `_id` value, with totals such as `$sum`.
`$sort` orders what it receives. Chapter 11 covers `$group` and the rest in depth.

steps.caption: The pipeline starts from the `books` collection: books by several authors.
`$match` keeps books from 1900 on. Emma, from 1815, is dropped.
`$group` makes one document per author. `books` counts that author's books with `$sum: 1`.
`$sort` with `-1` puts the author with the most books first.
`aggregate` resolves to an array of plain objects, not Mongoose documents.

code.title: Count books per author
code.caption: The same three stages, run for real. The loop shows how many documents each stage leaves.

walk.text: A bare schema, a connection and seven books by four authors.
A pipeline is an array. Each stage is an object with one `$` operator as its key.
`$match` keeps books from 1900 on, so Emma (1815) is dropped.
`$group` makes one document per author: `_id` is the author, `books` counts with `$sum: 1`.
`$sort` puts the author with the most books first.
Run the first stage, then the first two, then all three; print each count.
The full pipeline returns plain objects, one per author. Then disconnect.

pitfalls: `aggregate` does not cast: match an `_id` with `new mongoose.Types.ObjectId(id)`, not a string.
Results are plain objects, not Mongoose documents: they have no `save()`.
Put `$match` early: later stages then read fewer documents.

quiz.q: With the seven books from the example, what does this print?
quiz.why: `$match` runs first, before any document has a `books` field. Nothing matches, so `$group` gets no input.

takeaway: Stages run in order; each one sees only the previous stage's output.

starters: When should I use `aggregate` instead of `find`?
